value: estimated upper frequency limit of hearing 153 kHz, which the authors say was possibly an underestimate
method: auditory evoked potentials (click-evoked ABR and SAM-tone auditory steady-state response); threshold defined as the SPL of the lowest detected ASSR; upper frequency limit defined as the highest frequency corresponding to an interpolated threshold of 120 dB re 1 µPa
conditions: one neonate female pygmy sperm whale (SWCKb1701b, n=1) stranded on La Jolla Shores Beach, San Diego, California, on 28 July 2017 and tested at SeaWorld San Diego the following day, floating at the surface (no sedative stated); in poor health on admission and given ceftiofur, amikacin (cited by the authors as ototoxic, though judged unlikely to have affected the cochlea by test time) and enrofloxacin IM; died 23 August 2017; test frequencies 40, 56, 80, 113 and 160 kHz, so 153 kHz is interpolated below the highest tested; a full audiogram was not obtained; best sensitivity at 80 and 113 kHz, thresholds higher than in the dwarf sperm whale and higher than expected for similar-sized delphinids, and the authors cannot rule out underlying pathology affecting hearing; received levels for neonates likely underestimated (15 cm calibration distance); not a behavioural audiogram

source.authors: Houser DS, Noble L, Fougeres E, Mulsow J, Finneran JJ
source.title: Audiograms and click spectra of seven novel and seldom-tested odontocetes

quote: The estimated UFL was 153 kHz, although this was possibly an underestimate given that the thresholds appeared to be higher than expected for an animal of this age and size.
note: Name: Kogia breviceps in repo gbif-names.tsv (EXACT ACCEPTED). DOI checked on Crossref (title, five authors in this order, Frontiers in Marine Science vol 9, article 984333, issued 2022-12-21, CC BY 4.0 licence URL); the Frontiers PDF copy states CC BY. The quote was returned whole on one fetch and as two consecutive segments of the same sentence on a second fetch; the PDF copy was read through the fetch tool, which summarises text. The 153 kHz limit is one animal's estimate and a lower-confidence bound by the authors' own statement; the value carries only the 153 kHz limit and its qualifier. Same paper already supplies Kogia sima, Stenella frontalis, Peponocephala electra, Lissodelphis borealis and Feresa attenuata on main; Delphinus capensis from the same paper is held out (audit 286: California animals fall under Delphinus bairdii on MDD, which is not in gbif-names.tsv). Methods give poor health on admission, amikacin and death on 23 August 2017; the Discussion says underlying pathology affecting hearing cannot be ruled out, so the 153 kHz limit is one possibly impaired neonate's estimate, not a species limit.
